title: Regenerate functional human teeth in congenital tooth agenesis

concept.text: Induce development and eruption of missing permanent teeth with usable structure and occlusion. TRG035 entered human safety testing, but permission to run a trial is not approval of a tooth-regeneration treatment or proof of human regrowth. Proposed completion test: PMDA/MHLW or equivalent marketing authorization supported by controlled human evidence of new permanent-tooth formation and eruption, functional occlusion, and at least two years of dental safety and durability follow-up. Test set by: Proposed editorial clinical test; Japanese regulators would determine authorization. The first registered trial's primary endpoint is safety, not tooth regeneration. Overlaps: BME-11, PHA-12. Sources given: [Japanese official TRG035 trial registry](https://rctportal.mhlw.go.jp/en/detail?trial_id=jRCT2051240154) ; [Kitano Hospital explanation of the clinical programme](https://www.kitano-hp.or.jp/english/info/20240503?style=whats-new).

page.title: Tooth regeneration for congenital tooth agenesis
page.definition: A treatment causes permanent teeth to develop and emerge through the gum in people with congenital tooth agenesis, the developmental absence of teeth. The regenerated teeth participate in biting and chewing.

goal.need: A Japanese survey published in 2010 found congenitally missing permanent teeth, excluding third molars, in 1,568 of 15,544 paediatric dental patients (10.09%). This clinic sample is not a general-population prevalence estimate. The society's study links missing teeth to disturbed occlusion—the contact between upper and lower teeth—and subsequent skeletal and facial problems.

completion.title: MHLW grants marketing approval for a tooth-regeneration treatment for congenital tooth agenesis.
completion.criterion: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare grants product-specific marketing approval for treating congenital tooth agenesis through regeneration of missing permanent teeth, following review of the product's quality, efficacy and safety. The application must provide sufficient supporting evidence from ethical, scientific and reliable data. The regulator determines the indication-specific evidence required.
completion.set_by: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Approval Applications for Drugs, Section 1, paragraph 1, implementing Article 14; revision dated 9 October 2024.
completion.threshold_quote: Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare shall grant approval for each product based on the review.
completion.basis: Marketing approval supplies an existing external decision on a treatment's quality, efficacy and safety. This applies the general approval requirement to the tooth-regeneration indication. The notice supplies no tooth-specific threshold for eruption, functional occlusion or durability, and does not establish the draft's two-year follow-up requirement.

milestones.title: Normal third upper molars form in mice whose tooth development is genetically arrested.
milestones.criterion: The genetic-rescue experiment tests whether normal third maxillary molars form in Msx1-deficient mice when Usag-1 is also deleted. Histology at birth demonstrated these molars in all 3 double-mutant mice obtained among 151 littermates, reported on 12 February 2021. This is genetic rescue of developmental tooth absence.
milestones.set_by: Murashima-Suginami and colleagues, published genetic-rescue experiment in Science Advances, Figure 1; this test concerns a mouse model.
milestones.threshold_quote: all USAG-1−/−/Msx1−/− mice had normal third maxillary molar teeth

milestones.title: Nonclinical findings support a tooth-regeneration drug's proposed human dose and exposure duration.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical findings support the proposed initial human doses and exposure duration, as required by ICH E8(R1), section 4.2. Kitano Hospital reported completion of the required studies and PMDA consultation on 3 May 2024; that announcement provides no animal sample sizes or numerical acceptance limits and is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, ICH E8(R1), section 4.2; a general drug-development requirement applied here to tooth regeneration.
milestones.threshold_quote: sufficient non-clinical information to support initial human doses

milestones.title: TRG035 completes its registered Phase I single-dose safety study in adults.
milestones.criterion: Completion of jRCT2051240154, whose primary outcome is safety after one intravenous dose of TRG035 or placebo. The target is 30 men aged at least 30 and under 65 years, missing at least one molar, across 0.4, 1.2, 4.0, 12.0 and 24.0 mg/kg dose steps. The registry lists recruitment as complete. On 27 November 2025, Toregem reported study completion and confirmed safety; this is a company statement, not peer-reviewed evidence, and gives no detailed adverse-event results.
milestones.set_by: TRG035 study investigators, registered Phase I protocol jRCT2051240154; its primary endpoint is safety, without a publicly specified numerical safety pass criterion.

milestones.title: Treatment induces a missing permanent tooth to form in a person with congenital tooth agenesis.
milestones.criterion: At least one patient with documented congenital permanent-tooth absence develops a new permanent tooth after treatment. This is an Atlas minimum for human proof of concept, pending a public protocol-defined efficacy test. The announced TR-002 study targets 24 children with severe congenital partial anodontia and uses a non-comparative, open-label, multicentre design. Its non-peer-reviewed notice of 17 August 2026 reports completion of PMDA's notification review, with enrolment and dosing to follow ethics review; it reports no efficacy results.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback after searches of jRCT/NIPH, AMED, Kitano Hospital and Toregem for a published human tooth-formation success criterion; only a Phase IIa efficacy goal and study outline were located.

milestones.title: Confirmatory studies establish safety and efficacy of tooth regeneration in the intended patient population.
milestones.criterion: Confirmatory clinical studies establish that the tooth-regeneration treatment is safe and effective for its intended indication and patient population, providing an adequate basis for marketing approval. Endpoints must be clinically relevant or adequate surrogates. ICH E8(R1), section 4.3.2, sets this general standard but supplies no tooth-specific effect size or follow-up requirement. No confirmatory human efficacy results were located.
milestones.set_by: International Council for Harmonisation, ICH E8(R1), section 4.3.2; the general confirmatory-evidence standard, without a published tooth-regeneration protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: safe and effective for use for the intended indication and recipient population.

not_found: No tooth-specific regulatory or society threshold for eruption rate, functional occlusion or durability was found.
No public TR-002 registry record or full protocol defining its efficacy endpoint and success criterion was found.
No peer-reviewed human tooth-regeneration efficacy results or detailed Phase I safety results for TRG035 were found.
Direct access to jRCT2051240154 was blocked; its NIPH registry mirror was accessible.
No animal sample sizes or numerical acceptance limits for TRG035's completed regulatory nonclinical studies were located.
The publisher and PMC full-text routes for the 2021 paper were blocked; a PDF mirror was accessible.
